title: The last summer cover
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover is the four marks in the gravel where the chair was in June, the chair gone from them, in the shadow now. The owner asks where the chair is. Wood says in the shade. She says then it's fine. He says it's fine. The strip says it twice because it wants to be sure.

panels.composition: The cover: four small marks in gravel, sunlit, and the edge of a chair's shadow beside them.

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner. WOOD. BARNABY.

panels.composition: The owner looking at the marks. The strip looking at the owner.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner looking at a small drawing of marks in gravel, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The digest in the rack. The four marks facing the room. It's fine. The strip said so twice. Summer's done.
